messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] History of Stan
parts:
On Nov 5, 2016, at 7:54 AM, jt...@st-andrews.ac.uk wrote:

Hi,
 
I am trying to dig up some history on the development of Stan software (ie significant updates, motivation of developers who made it) to be included in my project write-up about Stan. 
Can anyone point me to a source I can look at?

There's a quick write up of the motivation and brief history at the start of the manual. 

If you want to see the actual source history, it's all there in git. It starts at GitHub.com/stan-dev/stan. I'm pretty sure when we migrated from Google code to GitHub, we were able to maintain our historical commits. (I could be wrong.) 

If you have specific questions, ask (here, on the users list)! The Stan team, on our webpage and manual, is listed in order of joining the team (almost: the first names joined at the start together in a sense).

If you're willing to dig, our development emails were moved to the stan-dev email list fairly early and some of us were big proponents of having as much communication be open as possible, so you can flip through the archive of that list and this list. 

Every release of Stan is on GitHub. We started CmdStan and RStan under one repo: look in the Stan releases. The manual was included in each and I believe full programs were in the manual starting pre-v1. 

And some of our examples in the example models have a long history. For example, dogs: https://github.com/stan-dev/example-models/commits/master/bugs_examples/vol1/dogs/dogs.stan

Hopefully that's enough info to get started. (I have a lot of this info off the top of my head because I'm preparing a talk that compares versions of Stan.)


Daniel




Yours,
Justin
